measurement_notes: Successful latency includes only responses marked success with no failed recorded assertion. A response with no assertions remains explicitly unasserted; it is not semantic proof.
HTTP 413/429, other resource errors, unsupported responses, assertion failures and other failures have separate latency distributions. Fast errors are never successful latency improvements.
Latency p95 uses nearest rank (ceil(0.95*n)); small sample sets are descriptive, not a throughput benchmark. Serial probes and concurrent groups are not pooled.

Primary hashes exclude only the recorded volatile paths. Secondary semantic hashes also exclude the recorded projection-context paths. A changed context requires an independent passing context assertion; hash equality does not replace identity, count, Session-membership or scalar assertions. An offline context proof compares a stored page context to the same-run direct probe with a recorded passing context assertion; it is explicitly distinguished from a runtime assertion on that page.

Memory is sampled before load, after concurrency groups and during idle. Sampled maxima can miss transient peaks. Cgroup usage includes file cache; working set is max(usage - inactive_file, 0), using total_inactive_file for cgroup v1 when present and inactive_file for v2.

Cgroup max_usage_in_bytes/peak is a cgroup-lifetime high-water mark, including startup, migration and earlier work unless separately reset. A persisted database cgroup can span baseline and candidate. Its peak is not a phase peak.

VmRSS and VmHWM are KiB from /proc. Summed current RSS can count shared pages more than once. VmHWM belongs to each process lifetime; the report never sums individual HWMs into a simultaneous peak. PIDs alone are not proof of process lifetime across restarts or PID reuse.

Synthetic same-VM evidence does not establish browser behavior, real external SDK compatibility, cold-start behavior, multi-day residency, distributed CE behavior or production-scale capacity. Per-run unrun fields remain authoritative.
